sections.title: ⚡ Claims — The Real Test of Insurance

cards.title: What is a Claim?
cards.content: A claim (called 'Dawa' in Hindi) is a formal request by the insured to the insurance company for compensation after a covered loss. The real test of any insurance company comes at the time of claim — it shows how efficiently the company honours its commitments.

cards.title: What is Loss Assessment?
cards.content: Loss Assessment is the process by which the insurance company determines: (1) Whether the loss is COVERED under the policy, (2) Whether the terms, conditions, and warranties have been VIOLATED or BREACHED, (3) Whether the claim is genuine and not fraudulent.

cards.title: What is TAT?
cards.content: TAT stands for TURNAROUND TIME. It is the time within which the insurance company must complete the loss assessment and process the claim. Standard claims must be paid within 30 DAYS as per IRDAI rules.

cards.title: What is Checked During TAT?
cards.content: During the Turnaround Time, the insurance company checks FOUR things: (1) Whether policy terms, conditions, and warranties have been breached, (2) Whether Utmost Good Faith has been followed, (3) Whether the loss falls within the scope (coverage) of the policy, (4) Whether the loss claimed is genuine and not fraudulent.

cards.title: 1. Standard Claims
cards.content: Standard Claims are those where: (1) The policy terms and conditions are clear, (2) No conditions or warranties have been breached by the insured. These claims are settled smoothly and quickly — WITHIN 30 DAYS as per IRDAI rules. These are the simplest category of claims.

cards.title: 2. Non-Standard Claims
cards.content: Non-Standard Claims are those where the insured has BREACHED (violated) the conditions, warranties, or terms of the policy. These claims take LONGER to settle because the insurance company conducts more detailed surveys and verifications. Compensation may be reduced or refused.

cards.title: 3. Act of God / Catastrophic Losses
cards.content: These are claims arising from NATURAL DISASTERS — storm, cyclone, flood, earthquake etc. (events caused by nature, not humans). In such cases, company surveyors reach the site QUICKLY, conduct thorough surveys, and assess all losses before processing the claim.

cards.title: What is Salvage?
cards.content: Salvage means the REMAINS or damaged property left after a loss has occurred (e.g., a wrecked car after an accident). After the insurer pays the claim, the salvage belongs to the INSURER (insurance company), not the insured.

cards.title: Salvage Belongs to — INSURER
cards.content: On payment of loss/claim — salvage belongs to the INSURER. This is the direct application of the Principle of Subrogation. Options to avoid: surveyor, local authorities, insured — all wrong. Correct answer is always the INSURER.

cards.title: Common Reasons for Claim Disputes
cards.content: Disputes between insurer and insured arise due to: (1) Delay in claim payment, (2) Complete rejection of the claim, (3) Claim admitted for a LESSER amount than what was claimed. When the insured is not satisfied, the matter goes to Grievance Redressal.

cards.title: Grievance Redressal and Ombudsman
cards.content: For insurance claim disputes, an OMBUDSMAN system and GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL mechanism has been set up by IRDAI. The insured can approach the ombudsman if unsatisfied with the insurer's response on their claim.

cards.title: Arbitration — Claim Dispute Resolution
cards.content: ARBITRATION is a method to resolve insurance claim disputes without going to court. An ARBITRATOR is chosen by BOTH parties (insurer and insured) with mutual consent. Arbitration is governed by the ARBITRATION AND CONCILIATION ACT, 1996. The arbitrator acts as a mediator and helps both parties reach a resolution.

cards.title: Motor Third Party Claims — Special Tribunal
cards.content: Motor Third Party claims are NOT settled in civil courts or through arbitration. They are settled through the MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL (MACT). This is a specialised tribunal established exclusively for motor accident related third-party claims.

cards.title: Who Investigates a Loss?
cards.content: Loss investigation (claims assessment) must be done by a LICENSED AND QUALIFIED SURVEYOR. An unlicensed surveyor, the insured's representative, or any random engineering graduate cannot conduct the official loss investigation.

cards.title: When is an Independent Surveyor Required?
cards.content: As per the Insurance Act, an INDEPENDENT SURVEYOR is required when the value of the claim is ABOVE Rs. 20,000. Below this threshold, the company's internal surveyor can handle it. (Note: IRDAI has proposed increasing this limit to Rs. 20,000+ in future but current exam answer is Rs. 20,000.)

cards.title: Claims Assessed Outside India (Travel Insurance)
cards.content: For Travel Insurance policies, if a claim arises OUTSIDE the country, it is assessed by the CLAIMS SETTLING AGENT named in the policy — not Indian surveyors, not the insurer's own employees. The policy document names the specific agent for overseas claim assessment.

cards.title: Fire Claim — Fire Brigade Report
cards.content: In case of a FIRE CLAIM, the report from the FIRE BRIGADE is NECESSARY (mandatory). The fire brigade arrives at a fire scene before the police, making their report the most critical document for fire claim processing.

cards.title: Personal Accident Claim — Doctor's Report
cards.content: For PERSONAL ACCIDENT CLAIMS, the report of a DOCTOR is mandatory. When an accident occurs, the first point of contact is medical assistance, making the doctor's report the essential document.

cards.title: Third Party Property Damage Claims — Survey Report
cards.content: Claims involving THIRD PARTY PROPERTY DAMAGE are assessed on the basis of the SURVEY REPORT prepared by the licensed surveyor who inspects the damage.

cards.title: Hit and Run Cases — Solatium Fund
cards.content: In HIT AND RUN cases where the vehicle that caused the accident cannot be identified, claims are settled from the SOLATIUM FUND (Solatium Scheme, 1989). This fund provides consolation compensation to victims (death or disability) when no insurance can be traced.

cards.title: When to Intimate a Loss
cards.content: The intimation of loss to the insurance company should be given AS SOON AS REASONABLY POSSIBLE after the loss occurs. Do not wait — early intimation enables faster claim processing. It should not be given 'at the exact time of loss' (impractical), nor delayed indefinitely.

cards.title: Benefit of Quick Claim Settlement
cards.content: If the insurer settles a claim quickly and efficiently, it acts as the BEST ADVERTISEMENT for the insurance company. Quick and fair claim settlement builds trust and reputation — it is the insurer's most powerful marketing tool.

cards.title: What is NOT Part of Professional Claim Settlement?
cards.content: Approaching a claim WITH PREJUDICE (bias, revenge, or malice) is NOT part of professional claim settlement. Professional settlement includes: collecting cause-of-loss information, checking if the loss is insured, and quantifying the claim amount. Prejudice has no place in this process.

sections.title: 🚀 Exam Pro-Tips — Chapter 6 (Quick Memory)
items: TAT = TURNAROUND TIME — time for loss assessment and claim processing.
Standard claims must be paid within 30 DAYS as per IRDAI rules.
TAT checks 4 things: breach of conditions, utmost good faith, scope of policy, fraud.
3 claim categories: Standard → Non-Standard → Act of God/Catastrophic.
Standard = no breach. Non-Standard = breach of conditions. Act of God = natural disaster.
Salvage (damaged property remains) belongs to INSURER after claim is paid.
Dispute causes: delay in payment, claim rejected, claim paid for lesser amount.
Arbitration = dispute resolution by mutually agreed Arbitrator. Governed by Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996.
Motor Third Party claims settled by MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL (MACT) — not civil court.
Loss investigation must be by LICENSED AND QUALIFIED SURVEYOR.
Independent Surveyor required if claim value exceeds Rs. 20,000.
Travel Insurance outside India: assessed by CLAIMS SETTLING AGENT named in the policy.
Fire claim: FIRE BRIGADE report is NECESSARY.
Personal Accident claim: DOCTOR's report is mandatory.
Third Party Property Damage: assessed on basis of SURVEY REPORT.
Hit and Run cases: claims from SOLATIUM FUND (Solatium Scheme, 1989).
Loss intimation to insurer: AS SOON AS REASONABLY POSSIBLE.
Quick claim settlement = BEST ADVERTISEMENT for insurer.
Approaching claim WITH PREJUDICE = NOT professional claim settlement.
